CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI V.HOSMANI  -3-  NC: 2026:KHC-D:3492  MFA No. 100980 of 2014 HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 02.12.2013 passed by Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Bailhongal ('Tribunal' for short) in MVC no.2765/2011, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Bailhongal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Sri SK Kayakamath, learned counsel for appellant submitted that, appeal was by insurer being aggrieved by finding of Tribunal regarding liability on insurer to pay compensation as well as on quantum of compensation.

It was submitted, on 23.05.2011 when claimant a student aged 12 years was playing by side of road near Grama Devi temple at Murgod village, rider of TVS CVTI motorcycle bearing temporary registration no.KA.22/TR-382 rode it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against claimant.
In said accident, claimant sustained fracture of first metatarsal bone.
Claiming compensation, she filed claim petition against owner and insurer of motorcycle under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act' for short) NC: 2026:KHC-D:3492 HC-KAR 3.
On appearance, claim petition was opposed on all counts.
4. Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
5. Father of claimant and Dr.C.D.Kulkarni, deposed as PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.17.

Respondent no.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R4.
6.

On consideration, Tribunal held accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by its rider and claimant was entitled for compensation Rs.1,80,810/- and held insurer liable to pay compensation.
Assailing said award on quantum as well as on liability, appeal was filed.

sentences.text: It was submitted, while there was no dispute about occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle leading to claimant sustaining injuries and physical disability, it was submitted as per Ex.P.6-charge sheet, rider NC: 2026:KHC-D:3492 HC-KAR and owner of offending vehicle were prosecuted for offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC read with Sections 3, 134, 187 of MV Act.
Specific contention was also taken by respondent-insurer about rider not having valid driving licence as on date of accident.

It was submitted, insurer had also filed IAs no.IV and V under Order 11 Rule 12 and 14 of CPC for a direction to rider and owner for production of driving licence of rider, which were allowed on 12.12.2012.
Despite same, owner failed to produce driving licence of rider.
Consequently, adverse inference ought to have been drawn by Tribunal that rider was not possessing valid and effective driving licence as on date of accident and absolved insurer from liability.
Failure to do so and fastening liability on surer was erroneous, illegal and called for interference.
8. On quantum it was submitted, claimant was 12 years of age as on date of accident and a non-earning person.

Such being case, Tribunal ought to have resorted to structured formula for assessment of compensation evolved NC: 2026:KHC-D:3492 HC-KAR in case of Master Mallikarjun V. Divisional Manager, the National Insurance Company Limited & another1

rather than,
determining compensation separately in each of head.
Alleging that there was award of excessive compensation and seeking for reduction, learned counsel prayed for allowing appeal.

9. Heard, learned counsel, perused impugned judgment, award and record.
10.

From above, and since insurer is in appeal challenging award not only on liability but also on quantum, points that would arise for consideration are:
"i.
Whether finding of Tribunal on liability of insurer to pay compensation is justified?
ii. Whether computation of compensation by Tribunal calls for modification?

11. Point no.1 : Ex.P.6-certified copy of charge sheet would reveal that rider of motorcycle was charge AIR 2014 Supreme Court 736 NC: 2026:KHC-D:3492 HC-KAR sheeted by police for offences not only of rash and negligent riding of motorcycle causing accident, but also for riding same without possessing valid and effective diving licence.
Further, as rightly submitted even owner failed to produce driving licence of rider of motorcycle even after allowing of IAs no.IV and V filed by insurer under Order XI Rule 12 and 14 of CPC.
Therefore adverse inference was required to be drawn.
While passing impugned award, Tribunal has not adverted to said aspect in detail.
Consequently misdirected itself in holding insurer liable to pay compensation.
However, it is seen that claimant in instant case is a third party.

12. Under such circumstances, as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in various decisions insurer at best would be required to pay compensation to claimant in first instance and thereafter seek reimbursement from owner/insured without requirement of separate proceedings.
Point no.1 is answered accordingly.

sentences.text: On quantum admittedly, claimant herein is a 12 years old student.
Taking note of difficulty to establish earning capacity of students/minors Hon'ble Supreme Court has evolved a structured formula for assessment of compensation under such cases.

As per ratio laid down,
claimant would require to establish injuries suffered as a result of negligence on part of rider/driver of offending vehicle, extent of disability sustained, quantum of medical expenses incurred and loss of income of parents during period of treatment.
Decision provided for lumpsum compensation towards pain and suffering, future loss of income and loss of amenities based on extent of disability sustained.
14. In instant case, Tribunal has assessed disability sustained by claimant to be at 6% to whole body.
Thus, claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under first slab.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3492 HC-KAR 15.
Apart from above, claimant would be entitled for Rs.21,930/- towards medical expenses, for which medical bills and prescriptions were produced as per Exs.P.12 and P13.
There is no specific material insofar as income of parents.
In absence, same has to be considered notionally.
Notional income for year 2011 is Rs.6,000/-.
Since claimant sustained fracture of metatarsal, which would normally heal within two months, claimant would be entitled to Rs.12,000/- towards loss of income of parents during laid up period.
Thus, total compensation would be as follows:

 up period  Total 1,33,930/-

 Reduction of compensation -46,880/-
16.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
- 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3492 HC-KAR ii.

with interest at rate of 6% per annum from date of petition, till deposit.
